headline: Pricing lifts profit, one-off charge drags earnings down
summary_short: Philip Morris International's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 10.4% y/y to $11.19B on pricing-led smoke-free growth, but net earnings fell 7.3% y/y to $2.82B (diluted EPS $1.80, -7.7%) after a $511M non-cash RBH impairment and unfavorable equity-investment swings.
summary_long: Net revenues of $11.19B (+10.4% y/y) were led by favorable international-combustibles pricing and smoke-free volume/mix (IQOS, VEEV), partly offset by softer U.S. volumes. Gross profit rose 11.5% y/y to $7.66B; operating income rose 22.0% y/y to $4.53B on pricing plus lower restructuring charges. Net earnings fell 7.3% y/y to $2.82B and diluted EPS fell 7.7% to $1.80, as a $511M non-cash RBH equity-investment impairment, unfavorable equity-security fair-value swings, and a higher effective tax rate (22.3% vs 19.0%) offset the operating gains. Cash rose to $6.00B; shareholders' equity stayed an $8.58B deficit. Management guided FY2026 capex to $1.4-1.6B and full-year effective tax rate near 21.5% ex-discrete items.
